## Auto Glass Association's post

### Auto Glass Association

6 May 2025  ·

U.S. Tariffs Hit the US Auto Glass Industry Hard

As the 25% import tariff on vehicles continues and new tariffs on auto parts take effect from May 3, the impact on the auto glass and repair industry is starting to bite. In a recent CIECA webinar, Mitchell’s Ryan Mandell outlined how the evolving trade environment is reshaping parts pricing and repair strategies—especially for glass and ADAS components. [...] With many aftermarket windshields sourced from China, auto glass is directly in the crosshairs. Mandell warns that while full vehicle prices may rise mid-year, glass and ADAS component prices could spike sooner.

Repairers are urged to audit their parts sourcing, anticipate price jumps, and consider more repairs over replacements where possible. The global supply chain isn't going back to "normal" anytime soon—being prepared is the best strategy.

This is good news for the automotive industry, Mandell says, because original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) like General Motors, Ford, Toyota, Nissan and Volkswagen “rely heavily” on Canada and Mexico for OEM and replacement parts.

The tariff effects vary based on what percentage of a vehicle’s parts are imports. Graph provided by Mitchell, an Enlyte company. U.S. Customs & Border Protection (CBP) recently published ruling HQ H315471 (Jun 28, 2023) in response to a request for Internal Advice (IA) regarding the Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS) classification for certain automotive glass. CBP specifically considered windshield glass, rear window glass and side window glass, all used for passenger vehicles of particular vehicle brands. The subject models were described as industry representatives and consisted of the following: [...] and were more properly classified in subheading 7007.11.10 which provides for “Safety glass, consisting of toughened (tempered) or laminated glass: Toughened (tempered) safety glass: Of size and shape suitable for incorporation in vehicles, aircraft, spacecraft or vessels: For motor vehicles of chapter 87.” This is subject to a duty rate of 5.5%. results.title: Understanding the New Tariffs and their Potential Impact ...
results.content: China faces a more unique situation. In January, President Trump imposed a 20 percent tariff on all goods from China. That means that a windshield wiper manufactured in China will face a 45 percent import tariff starting on May 3. A microwave made in China will be subject to a 54 percent rate starting on April 9. Meanwhile, a tail light produced entirely in Mexico will not face any tariff. President Trump reserves the right to expand or pull back these tariffs when he deems appropriate, as he [...] On March 26, the Trump Administration announced a 25 percent tariff on imports of automobiles and certain automotive parts. The tariff went into effect for fully assembled vehicles on April 3. The tariff on auto parts will go into effect on May 3. The original order only applied the tariff on auto parts that fit the following categories: engines and engine parts; transmissions and powertrains; and electrical components. Since then, that list has been updated to include 150 categories, including [...] of 25% tariffs on automobile and automobile parts imports, and the across-the-board tariffs announced yesterday, the reports’ findings and recommendations are materializing in tangible policy changes that could impact how auto repairers operate their businesses.
